summary: Defines xCal, an XML representation of iCalendar data. It lets calendar information that normally uses the text iCalendar format be exchanged as XML.

plainLanguage.summary: xCal represents iCalendar calendar data as XML. It maps the calendar's parts into XML elements so data can be converted back to iCalendar with the same meaning.

questions: how to convert icalendar to xml
subtitle: Maps iCalendar calendar data into XML while preserving its meaning when converted back.

tldr.problem: Applications that exchange calendar data in iCalendar need a specialized parser, while XML tools are widely available for processing structured data.
tldr.mechanism: xCal maps calendar components, properties, parameters and values to XML elements, with defined handling for special properties and unknown values.
tldr.outcome: A conforming xCal document can be converted back to semantically equivalent iCalendar data. RFC 6321 is updated by RFC 6868 and RFC 7529.

today: RFC 6321 is a Proposed Standard published in August 2011. It has been updated by RFC 6868 and RFC 7529, and has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Why iCalendar Has an XML Mapping
sections.content:
iCalendar is a widely used exchange format for calendar and scheduling data, but applications need a dedicated parser and generator for it. XML has tools for generating, parsing and manipulating structured data.

xCal defines a direct mapping from iCalendar to XML. The design aims to preserve components, properties and parameters when converting to xCal and back, except where values are defaults. xCal preserves iCalendar meaning; fully understanding or changing the data still requires knowledge of iCalendar.
sections.plainLanguage: xCal gives calendar data an XML form while keeping its iCalendar meaning. Converting the data back should preserve its components, properties and parameters.

sections.title: Mapping Calendar Objects to Elements
sections.content:
Before conversion, folded iCalendar lines MUST be unfolded and text escapes MUST be removed. An entire iCalendar stream becomes an icalendar root element. Each calendar object becomes vcalendar, with components inside components and properties inside properties.

Each component, property and parameter becomes an element with the corresponding name in lowercase. A property contains its value elements and may contain a parameters element. The VALUE parameter is omitted because the value element's name identifies the type.
sections.plainLanguage: The XML uses nested elements for the calendar, its components, and their properties. Names match iCalendar names in lowercase, and a value element shows the property's data type.

sections.title: Special Properties and Value Types
sections.content:
Several multi-valued properties, including CATEGORIES, RESOURCES, FREEBUSY, EXDATE and RDATE, become elements with multiple value elements. GEO becomes separate latitude and longitude elements. REQUEST-STATUS becomes code, description and, when present, data elements.

Value types have matching lowercase element names such as text, date, date-time, duration and recur. Dates use hyphens and times use colons. Time-zone information continues to use the iCalendar TZID parameter. Binary data is represented as base64 in a binary element.
sections.plainLanguage: Most values use a matching element name, while a few properties are split into parts. Dates and times use XML-style separators, and the format preserves iCalendar's time-zone parameter.

sections.title: Converting xCal Back to iCalendar
sections.content:
When converting back, component, property and parameter names SHOULD be written in uppercase, following common iCalendar practice. The converter MUST apply iCalendar text escaping and line folding.

Because xCal represents value types with different XML elements, it does not include the iCalendar VALUE parameter in the XML. When creating iCalendar, the converter MUST add VALUE if the property's value type is not its default type. Non-binary values MUST NOT be base64 encoded.
sections.plainLanguage: To return to iCalendar, the converter writes the names in the usual uppercase form and restores required escaping and line folding. It also adds VALUE when the type is not the property's default.

sections.title: Extensions and Unknown Values
sections.content:
iCalendar extension properties and parameters with an X- prefix map to lowercase XML element names using the same rule as standard names. An extension element in the iCalendar XML namespace must begin with x-. XML in another namespace can be preserved in iCalendar through the XML property under the conditions in the RFC.

If a converter does not recognize a property or parameter and cannot determine its default type, xCal uses an unknown value element containing the unprocessed text. Converting it back preserves that text directly.
sections.plainLanguage: Unknown values are kept in an element marked unknown instead of being discarded. This lets a converter pass the original text through when it creates iCalendar again.

sections.title: Security and Registrations
sections.content:
The mapping itself introduces no new security concerns related to calendar data; the RFC points readers to the iCalendar specification for those. XML has separate security risks, which the RFC directs readers to the XML guidance it cites.

The RFC registers the XML namespace urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:icalendar-2.0, the application/calendar+xml media type and the iCalendar property XML. The media type uses the file extension xcs.
sections.plainLanguage: Calendar-data security remains covered by iCalendar, while XML brings its own security guidance. The RFC registers the xCal namespace, media type and XML property.
